subtitle: When the Victor Chose Restraint at Kanchi

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a crowned king before distant temple towers
panels.action: Vikramaditya II stands in gleaming mail with hand resting lightly on his sheathed sword, gazing toward the soaring stone gopuras of Kanchipuram under a hazy southern sky.

dialogue.text: In the age of Badami’s Chalukyas, Vikramaditya II rode to Kanchi and carved his glory not in ruin, but in restraint.

i18n.hi: बदामी के चालुक्यों के युग में विक्रमादित्य द्वितीय कांची पहुँचा, और अपना यश विनाश नहीं, संयम में गढ़ गया।

panels.shot: epic bird's-eye over Deccan plateau with distant city
panels.action: From a high vantage, Vikramaditya II is seen on horseback amidst his retinue, the rocky ridges and temple-dotted plains of the Deccan stretching toward the fortified skyline of Badami.

dialogue.text: From the red cliffs of Badami, the Chalukya kings watched the south, where Pallava Kanchi shone like a rival sun.

i18n.hi: बदामी की लाल चट्टानों से चालुक्य राजे दक्षिण को निहारते, जहाँ पल्लवों की कांची प्रतिद्वन्द्वी सूरज-सी चमकती थी।

panels.shot: medium interior shot in royal hall, slight low angle
panels.action: In a pillared hall at Badami, Vikramaditya II sits straight-backed on a low throne, battle maps spread before him, courtiers and generals standing in attentive silence.

dialogue.text: Decades earlier, Pulakeshin II had fallen to the Pallavas. The wound lingered; a son must answer where a father had failed.

i18n.hi: कुछ दशक पहले पुलकेशी द्वितीय पल्लवों से हार चुका था। घाव बचा था; जहाँ पिता चूका, पुत्र को जवाब देना था।

panels.shot: close-up on Vikramaditya II’s face over the maps
panels.action: Vikramaditya II leans over a palm-leaf map marked with routes toward Kanchipuram, his eyes calm yet intent, fingers resting on the Pallava capital’s symbol.

dialogue.speaker: vikramaditya_ii
dialogue.text: We ride not for rage alone, but for memory and measure.

i18n.hi: हम केवल क्रोध से नहीं, स्मृति और संतुलन से सवार हैं।

panels.shot: sweeping wide shot of marching army on dusty road
panels.action: Vikramaditya II rides at the head of a disciplined column of cavalry and infantry, war elephants looming behind, their banners bearing the Chalukya emblem as dust rises in the morning light.

dialogue.text: Between c. 731 and 740, his armies pressed south thrice, crossing rivers and ridges toward the famed city of Kanchi.

i18n.hi: लगभग ७३१ से ७४० के बीच उसकी सेनाएँ तीन बार दक्षिण उतरीं, नदियाँ-पहाड़ पार कर कांची की ओर बढ़ते हुए।

panels.shot: medium shot at a river crossing, side angle
panels.action: At a broad riverbank, Vikramaditya II watches as soldiers ford the waters, elephants stepping carefully, the reflection of his horse and armor shimmering in the current.

dialogue.text: The Kauthem copper plates remember these marches, grants of land forged in the shadow of war.

i18n.hi: कौठेम की ताम्रपत्रियाँ इन चढ़ाइयों को याद रखती हैं, युद्ध की छाया में मिली भूमि की दानपत्रें।

panels.shot: wide shot of Kanchipuram skyline from a distance
panels.action: From a hill outside the city, Vikramaditya II and his officers gaze upon Kanchipuram’s skyline, its layered temple towers and defensive walls rising above groves and tanks.

dialogue.text: Kanchi, seat of the Pallavas, was more than a fortress. It was a city of stone hymns, of scholars and shrines.

i18n.hi: कांची, पल्लवों की राजधानी, केवल किला नहीं थी; वह पत्थर की स्तुतियों, विद्वानों और देवालयों का नगर था।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-wide at city gate, frontal angle
panels.action: At a massive city gate half-open, Vikramaditya II stands poised, his troops streaming past into Kanchipuram, while a few defeated Pallava guards stand aside, disarmed and wary.

dialogue.text: The Pallava power bent before him. Victory opened the gates, and with them, the peril of pride.

i18n.hi: पल्लव शक्ति उसके आगे झुक गई। विजय ने फाटक खोले, और साथ ही घमंड का ख़तरा।

panels.shot: interior wide of Kailasanatha temple courtyard
panels.action: Within the Kailasanatha temple courtyard, Vikramaditya II walks slowly, helm removed, as he looks up at the sculpted tower; Chalukya soldiers stand respectfully at a distance amid carved lions and stone pillars.

dialogue.text: In the Kailasanatha temple, a Pallava jewel of stone, the conqueror entered as a guest beneath another king’s artistry.

i18n.hi: कैलासनाथ मन्दिर में, पल्लवों के इस रत्न-से पत्थर में, विजेता दूसरे राजा की कलाकारी के नीचे अतिथि बनकर प्रविष्ट हुआ।

panels.shot: close-up on sculpted wall with Vikramaditya II in profile
panels.action: Side by side with a richly carved relief of Shiva, Vikramaditya II is seen in profile, his gaze tracing the chiselled forms, his expression a mix of admiration and resolve.

dialogue.speaker: vikramaditya_ii
dialogue.text: Steel can break stone, but it cannot carve like this.

i18n.hi: लोहे की धार पत्थर तोड़ सकती है, पर ऐसी नक्काशी नहीं कर सकती।

panels.shot: medium shot of Vikramaditya II addressing officers inside temple
panels.action: In the pillared mandapa, Vikramaditya II turns to his officers, raising an open hand to halt them, while a few nervous attendants clutch temple lamps nearby.

dialogue.text: Here, where a lesser man might boast in ashes, he set a different command.

i18n.hi: यहाँ, जहाँ कोई तुच्छ पुरुष राख पर इतराता, उसने अलग आज्ञा दी।

panels.shot: tight medium on Vikramaditya II, slight low angle
panels.action: Vikramaditya II stands firm, one hand on his sword hilt but not drawing it, the other gesturing toward the sanctum as his generals listen, their faces lit by oil lamps.

dialogue.speaker: vikramaditya_ii
dialogue.text: Let no shrine be harmed, no image carried away. Our fame needs no theft.

i18n.hi: कोई मन्दिर न टूटे, कोई प्रतिमा न उठाई जाए। हमारे यश को चोरी की ज़रूरत नहीं।

panels.shot: close-up on a stone pillar being inscribed
panels.action: A sculptor-scribe kneels at a tall stone pillar in the temple, carefully chiselling a line of Nagari script, while Vikramaditya II stands in the background, watching silently.

dialogue.text: On a pillar of Kailasanatha, his men cut words instead of wounds, an inscription of victory without desecration.

i18n.hi: कैलासनाथ के एक स्तम्भ पर उसके सैनिकों ने घाव नहीं, शब्द गढ़े—अपमान के बिना विजय की लेख

panels.shot: extreme close-up of inscription line with shadowed profile
panels.action: The freshly carved inscription line is shown in sharp detail, Vikramaditya II’s shadow falling across the stone as if sealing the words with his presence.

dialogue.text: It declared that the Chalukya had entered, triumphed, and yet had not seized the temples’ wealth nor scarred their walls.

i18n.hi: उसने घोषित किया कि चालुक्य आया, जीता, पर न तो मन्दिरों का धन लूटा, न उनकी दीवारों पर घाव छोड़े।

panels.shot: wide shot of city street with temples intact
panels.action: A broad street of Kanchipuram is shown with its shrines and houses intact, townsfolk cautiously emerging as Chalukya soldiers march past in order, keeping distance from the sacred enclosures.

dialogue.text: Kanchi did not fall into ruin. Its towers still caught the sun; its lanes still hummed, though under a stranger’s gaze.

i18n.hi: कांची खंडहर नहीं बनी। उसके शिखर अभी सूरज थामते रहे, उसकी गलियाँ अब भी गूँजती रहीं, बस अजनबी नज़र के साये में।

panels.shot: medium shot of Vikramaditya II taking leave of Kanchi
panels.action: At the edge of Kanchipuram, Vikramaditya II turns his horse away from the city, pausing for a last look at its temples before leading his column back toward the Deccan.

dialogue.text: He did not make Kanchi his seat. The city remained Pallava at heart, yet now carried a Chalukya’s memory on its stone.

i18n.hi: उसने कanchi को अपनी राजधानी नहीं बनाया। नगर दिल से पल्लव ही रहा, पर अब उसकी शिला पर चालुक्य की स्मृति भी अंकित थी।

panels.shot: epic wide of Pattadakal temple complex under construction
panels.action: In the riverine plain of Pattadakal, Vikramaditya II stands overseeing artisans lifting stone blocks, emerging temples rising with mixed styles as the Malaprabha river glitters beyond.

dialogue.text: Back in the Deccan, at Pattadakal, new shrines rose. Scholars see in their forms the echo of Kanchi, victory translated into stone.

i18n.hi: दक्खिन लौटकर पट्टदकल में नये मन्दिर उठे। विद्वान उनकी रेखाओं में कांची की गूँज देखते हैं—विजय पत्थर में रूपान्तरित।

panels.shot: close-up on sculptor and Vikramaditya II observing a relief
panels.action: A sculptor chisels a relief on a Pattadakal wall while Vikramaditya II watches thoughtfully, his hand tracing the outline of a motif reminiscent of southern temples.

dialogue.text: Stones remember exchanges that chronicles forget. Influence traveled with armies, not only as spoil, but as inspiration.

i18n.hi: पत्थर वे सौदे याद रखते हैं जिन्हें इतिहास भूल जाता है। असर सेनाओं के साथ चलता है, लूट नहीं, प्रेरणा बनकर भी।

panels.shot: low-angle medium of Vikramaditya II against sky and temple silhouettes
panels.action: Vikramaditya II stands framed against the sky, Pattadakal’s clustered shikharas behind him, his face grave yet serene as if listening to distant temple bells.

dialogue.text: Vikramaditya II’s boast at Kanchi was rare: that he spared. In an age of conquest, his name endures where the victor chose to leave another’s gods unbroken.

i18n.hi: कanchi में विक्रमादित्य द्वितीय का दुर्लभ दम्भ यही था: कि उसने बख्शा। विजय के युग में उसका नाम वहाँ टिका है, जहाँ विजेता ने पराये देवों को अटूट छोड़ा।

title_i18n.hi: विक्रमादित्य द्वितीय ने कांची के मन्दिरों को छोड़ा

subtitle_i18n.en: When the Victor Chose Restraint at Kanchi
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब विजेता ने कांची में संयम चुना
